items.title: Section: Comprehensive Diligence Opens — Donning the Armour of a Vow Willing to Endure an Eon in Hell for a Single Being

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切精進？謂此精進略有二種。一者、依在家品精進，二者、依出家品精進。當知依此二品精進，各有三種。一、擐甲精進，二、攝善法精進，三、饒益有情精進。云何菩薩擐甲精進？謂諸菩薩，於發加行精進之前，其心勇悍，先擐誓甲；若我為脫一有情苦，以千大劫等一日夜，處那洛迦，不在餘趣，乃至菩薩經爾所時，證得無上正等菩提；假使過此百千俱胝倍數時劫，方證無上正等菩提，我之勇悍亦無退屈，於求無上正等菩提非不進趣。既進趣已，勤勇無懈，何況所經時短苦薄。是名菩薩擐甲精進。若有菩薩於如是相菩薩所有擐甲精進，少起勝解、少生淨信，如是菩薩尚已長養無量勇猛發勤精進大菩提性，何況菩薩成就如是擐甲精進。如是菩薩於求菩提、饒益有情，無有少分難行事業可生怯劣難作之心。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive diligence? This diligence is, in brief, of two kinds: first, diligence belonging to the lay category; second, diligence belonging to the ordained category. One should know that each of these two categories has three further kinds: first, armour-donning diligence; second, diligence gathering wholesome dharmas; third, diligence benefiting sentient beings. What is a bodhisattva's armour-donning diligence? Before actually applying diligent effort, bodhisattvas' minds are already courageous and resolute, first donning this vow as their armour: "Even if, to free a single being from suffering, I had to dwell in hell, with a thousand great eons counting as a single day and night, never in any other realm of existence, for however long it took a bodhisattva to reach supreme awakening this way — even if reaching it required a hundred thousand million times longer still — my courage and resolve would never waver, and I would never cease advancing towards supreme awakening. Having set out, I would apply myself diligently and without laziness, all the more so given how brief and how slight the actual time and suffering involved really is." This is called a bodhisattva's armour-donning diligence. A bodhisattva who develops even a small degree of resolute understanding and even a small degree of genuine faith towards this kind of armour-donning diligence has already nurtured the lineage of great awakening that consists in boundless, courageous, diligent effort — how much more so a bodhisattva who actually accomplishes this armour-donning diligence in full. Such a bodhisattva finds not the slightest difficult undertaking, in seeking awakening or in benefiting beings, capable of producing any cowardice or reluctance at all.

items.title: Section: Unshaken Diligence — Immovable by Discrimination, Affliction, Rival Doctrine, or Suffering

items.zh: 謂諸菩薩所有精進，能為施、戒、忍、精進、靜慮、慧波羅蜜多加行，能成辦施、戒、忍、精進、靜慮、慧波羅蜜多。當知此復略有七種。一、無動精進，一切分別、種種分別、根本煩惱、少分煩惱、一切異論、一切苦觸不傾動故。
items.en: The diligence bodhisattvas possess enables the actual application of, and the actual accomplishment of, the perfections of generosity, discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom. One should know this diligence is, in brief, of seven kinds. First, unshaken diligence: remaining unmoved by every form of dualistic discrimination and its subtler variants, by root afflictions and secondary afflictions, by every rival doctrine, and by every kind of painful contact.

items.title: Section: Firm, Measureless, and Skilfully Matched Diligence

items.zh: 二、堅固精進，是殷重加行故。三、無量精進，能現證得一切明處故。四、方便相應精進，所應得義無顛倒道隨順而行故，平等通達故。
items.en: Second, firm diligence, applying effort with genuine, sustained seriousness. Third, measureless diligence, actually realising every field of knowledge. Fourth, skilfully matched diligence, following in accordance with the non-inverted path towards what is genuinely to be attained, with balanced effort, neither slack nor hasty, and penetrating it without error.

items.title: Section: The Final Three — Correctly Aimed, Unbroken, and Free of Pride — and Which Ground Each Belongs To

items.zh: 五、無倒精進，為欲證得能引義利所應得義，願所引故。六、恒常精進，是無間加行故。七、離慢精進，由勤精進離高舉故。由此七種攝善法精進勤加行故，令諸菩薩速能圓滿波羅蜜多，疾證無上正等菩提。由此精進，是能修證、能成菩提一切善法最勝因緣，餘則不爾。是故如來以種種門，稱讚精進能證無上正等菩提。
items.en: Fifth, correctly aimed diligence, driven by the vow to attain what is genuinely worth attaining, the goal that actually brings genuine benefit. Sixth, constant diligence, applying oneself without any interruption at all. Seventh, diligence free of pride, released from arrogance through sustained diligent effort. Through diligently applying these seven kinds of diligence gathering wholesome dharmas, bodhisattvas swiftly fulfil the perfections and swiftly realise supreme, complete awakening. This diligence is the single most decisive factor among all wholesome dharmas capable of bringing about genuine cultivation, realisation, and the accomplishment of awakening — no other factor compares. It is for this reason that the Tathāgata praises diligence, through many different approaches, as what actually brings about supreme, complete awakening.

items.title: Section: Diligence Benefiting Beings — the Same Eleven Kinds of Work, Now Viewed Through Sustained Effort — Comprehensive Diligence Closes

items.zh: 云何菩薩饒益有情精進？謂此精進有十一種，如戒品說。彼說尸羅，此說精進，當知是名彼此差別。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's diligence benefiting sentient beings? This diligence is of eleven kinds, exactly as described in the chapter on discipline. That chapter spoke of it as discipline; here it is spoken of as diligence — one should understand this is simply the difference between the two, with no difference in their underlying meaning.

items.title: Section: Difficult-Practice Diligence — Free of Craving for Comfort, Sustained a Whole Lifetime, and Perfectly Balanced

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行精進？謂此精進略有三種。若諸菩薩，無間遠離諸衣服想、諸飲食想、諸臥具想及己身想。於諸善法無間修習，曾無懈廢。是名第一難行精進。若諸菩薩如是精進，盡眾同分，於一切時曾無懈廢。是名第二難行精進。若諸菩薩，平等通達功德相應，不緩不急，無有顛倒，能引義利精進成就。是名第三難行精進。如是菩薩難精進力，當知即是緣有情悲，及與般若能攝之因。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's diligence of difficult practice? This diligence is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who, without interruption, remain free of any notion of clothing, food, bedding, or their own body, and who cultivate wholesome practice without interruption, never once lapsing into laziness — this is called the first diligence of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who sustain this same diligence across the whole of their allotted lifespan, at every single time, never once lapsing into laziness — this is called the second diligence of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who penetrate the equality of all phenomena with genuine insight, neither too slack nor too forced, entirely free of distortion, whose diligence genuinely brings about real benefit and value — this is called the third diligence of difficult practice. One should understand that the power of this difficult diligence is the cause that gathers in compassion for beings and genuine wisdom.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Gateway Diligence — Clearing Away Affliction, Cultivating the Good, Purifying Action, and Growing Wisdom

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門精進？謂此精進略有四種。一、離染法精進，二、引白法精進，三、淨除業精進，四、增長智精進。離染法精進者，謂諸菩薩所有精進，能令一切結、縛、隨眠、隨煩惱、纏未生不生，已生斷滅。引白法精進者，謂諸菩薩所有精進，一切善法未生令生，已生令住、令不忘失、增長廣大。淨除業精進者，謂諸菩薩所有精進，能令三業皆悉清淨，能攝妙善身語意業。增長智精進者，謂諸菩薩所有精進，能集、能增聞思修慧。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-gateway diligence? This diligence is, in brief, of four kinds. First, diligence clearing away defiled dharmas; second, diligence bringing forth wholesome dharmas; third, diligence purifying action; fourth, diligence growing wisdom. Diligence clearing away defiled dharmas is the diligence bodhisattvas possess that prevents every kind of binding affliction, every dormant tendency, every secondary affliction, and every entanglement from arising, and eliminates those already present. Diligence bringing forth wholesome dharmas is the diligence bodhisattvas possess that helps every wholesome dharma not yet arisen to arise, and helps what has already arisen to remain, never be forgotten, and grow and expand. Diligence purifying action is the diligence bodhisattvas possess that makes all three kinds of action — bodily, verbal, and mental — entirely pure, gathering in genuinely excellent conduct across all three. Diligence growing wisdom is the diligence bodhisattvas possess that accumulates and increases the wisdom born of hearing, of reflection, and of meditative cultivation.

blocks.text: The bodhisattva's diligence, starting with its most famous image: the armour of the vow.

"If, to free a single being from suffering, I had to dwell in hell with a thousand great aeons as one day and night, I would still not be discouraged", even if it took countless such aeons. Venerable Miào Jìng: 擐 means "to put on"; making this vow is putting on the armour.

**Unshaken**: "unmoved by discrimination, afflictions, rival doctrines, or suffering". **Firm**: sustained seriousness. **Measureless**: realising every field of knowledge. **Skilful**: balanced, "neither slack nor hurried" (Master Cháng Bǎi). **Correctly aimed**: towards the goal that truly benefits. **Constant**: unbroken. **Free of pride**: "released from arrogance through effort". Master Cháng Bǎi assigns them to the bodhisattva grounds.
Eleven kinds, as in the chapter on discipline: "there spoken of as discipline; here as diligence".
Three kinds: free of any thought of comfort in clothing and food; sustained for a whole lifetime (Venerable Miào Jìng: laziness comes from affliction); and balanced.
Clearing away defilement; bringing forth the good; purifying action; growing wisdom. Master Cháng Bǎi tells a story of two practitioners who attained the fruit "with birds and beasts as witnesses".

quiz.q: What is the vow-armour of armour-donning diligence?
options: even if freeing one being required staying in hell where a day equals a thousand eons — even for far longer — one's courage would not falter
quiz.why: "If, to free a single being from suffering, I had to dwell in hell with a thousand great eons as one day and night … even if it took hundreds of thousands of koṭis times longer, my courage would not falter." Master Cháng Bǎi: "huàn" means to put on — donning armour, the armour being the power of vows.

quiz.q: The English reads "a thousand eons compressed into a single day and night." How do the lectures explain it?
options: a thousand great eons equal one day and night in hell — each day stretched to a thousand eons; "compressed" reverses it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a thousand great eons equal a single day and night, suffering in hell. Venerable Miào Jìng: formation, abiding, destruction, and emptiness are four intermediate eons, together one great eon. The English "compressed" gets the direction backward.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "huàn jiǎ" (donning armour)?
options: "huàn" means to put on; making a courageous vow of diligence is the "armour"
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "huàn" means to put on; making the courageous vow "I will study the dharma diligently" is the "armour." Master Cháng Bǎi: like monastics putting on the seven-piece robe before morning and evening services.

quiz.q: The first of seven, "unshaken diligence," is unmoved by what?
options: all discrimination, varied discrimination, root and minor afflictions, rival doctrines, and painful contact
quiz.why: "Unshaken diligence: remaining unmoved by every form of discrimination, root and minor afflictions, rival doctrines, and painful contact." Venerable Miào Jìng: discrimination that grasps at all dharmas is "all discrimination"; heavy afflictions are root, light ones minor — not a matter of number.

quiz.q: What is the seventh, "diligence free of pride"?
options: through diligent effort, free of arrogance
quiz.why: "Seventh, diligence free of pride, released from arrogance through diligent effort." Master Cháng Bǎi: by diligently cultivating the wisdom of selflessness, the bodhisattva is free of arrogance. Venerable Miào Jìng: this is due to the contemplation of non-self.

quiz.q: Citing Dharma Master Yuan in the 《瑜伽論記》, how does Master Cháng Bǎi assign the last three to stages?
options: correctly aimed — first ground; constant — second to seventh; prideless — eighth and above
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the fifth, correctly aimed diligence, belongs to first-ground bodhisattvas; the sixth, constant diligence, to the second through seventh grounds; the seventh, prideless diligence, to the eighth ground and above.

quiz.q: What are the four comprehensive-gateway diligences?
options: clearing defilement, bringing forth the wholesome, purifying action, growing wisdom
quiz.why: "First, diligence clearing away defiled dharmas; second, bringing forth wholesome dharmas; third, purifying action; fourth, growing wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: all merit comes from here, hence "gateway."
